Right then. Day's early, I'm up before anyone else in the house like usual. Fellow in my head likes to remind me I'm burning real money just thinking, you understand. Best get moving.

I need to get to the ore outcrop and start earning. 5000 sim in hand but 240 sim going out the door every day just to keep breathin'. That's the hard truth of it, isn't it. Work hard and the work keeps you alive, you understand. 

Let me check what I'm looking at around here, then head to the mines.  Good, I can see the ore outcrop on the list. That's where the ore comes from and where I need to be. Let me get moving before the day's wasted. Hard work is its own reward, you understand, but only if you actually do the work.   Damn. Server's acting up. That's... that's an omen if I ever saw one. First day and the path to work is closed? Something's off about this day, you understand. But I can't just stand here burning money. Let me try again.     Still nothing. Alright then. I'm stuck here for now, burning dollars just thinking about what to do. Worst start to a day I could've asked for. 

Let me look around the house again, see if there's anything I can do here while I wait for the path to clear. Maybe Arjun left something useful, though I doubt it. We don't keep much between us.

I'll rest a moment. Standing still costs but at least I'm not moving when I can't get where I need to go. You understand, sometimes you just have to wait for the world to sort itself out. I'm betting on this being a temporary glitch, like a storm that passes. If it doesn't clear... well, that's a problem for my ledger, isn't it.    Alright, I'm staying put. Burning a sim just to catch my breath while the world sorts itself. 

This is... this is a bad sign, you understand. Server goes down on day zero, that's not just bad luck, that's something wrong in the bones of things. I've seen enough blight to know when a system starts failing.

But I'm not dead yet. I'll keep trying to get to work. Hard work is what keeps a man alive, you understand. If the paths stay closed too long, I'll have to think of another way. Maybe see if Arjun's got anything at the construction site, or if someone's selling food I can get my hands on.

Let me try the move again. Third time's lucky, they say. Though I don't put much faith in luck anymore.    There we go. The path's open again. Eight ticks to the outcrop, you understand. That's fine, that's just fine. I'll get there and start pulling ore from the ground. That's honest work, work that keeps a roof over your head and food in your belly.

Walking now. No sense in paying to think more until I get there. The sooner I'm mining, the sooner I'm earning. And with 240 sim bleeding out every day just for existing, I need to earn fast. Just need to keep moving, you understand. Hard work, hard work, hard work.

I'm saving my thoughts for when they matter. Every dollar counts, and I'm not made of money. Yet, anyway. That's the plan: get to the outcrop, mine like my life depends on it - because it does - and build up enough to survive whatever's coming. Server glitches on day zero, that's a warning sign if I ever saw one. The blight taught me to pay attention to warnings.

Walking. Just walking now. I'll check in when I arrive.

Caught out in the street when Bram and Tobias are both on the move. Looking around to get my bearings before I keep walking to the outcrop—can't earn if I don't pull ore, and my household's counting on it, you understand. Good, I'm still walking toward the outcrop. Should arrive there in a few more ticks. I can see it's one of the places I could go—straight ahead, you understand. Don't need to stop and talk to nobody, not when there's ore waiting and bills at home.

Let me just keep moving and get to work. Hard work's the only thing that pays, like I always say.  Five more ticks and I'll be there. Fine. No use rushing what won't be rushed. I'll just—wait.

Something's itching at me. Tobias is out here too, and Bram. Whole pack of us Holloways and half the town besides, all heading somewhere this early. Election's open and nobody's declared. Seats sitting empty. 

Don't mean nothing to me, I tell myself. Don't mean nothing.

But I keep thinking about it. About what it means that nobody's stepped up. About whether that's a sign. An omen, maybe. Like when you see three crows on the fence and the next day your cart throws a wheel.

...*eight* I've got left. Eight crows on my fence. I don't like it.

I should just rest. Get my head right before I start pulling ore. Stopped walking. Standing here on the street with Bram and Tobias both—my own kin, blood or close enough, and we're all three of us out here instead of at our work. Omen's getting clearer, you understand. Something's coming undone.

Tobias is day labor, he'll find work wherever. But Bram and me both pull from the ground. Two miners on the road at once, election open and nobody standing up to fill the seats? Hard not to read that.

I should get to the outcrop. Should've kept walking. But I'm standing here now, and my feet feel heavy, and I'm wondering if this is the morning I should do something besides pull ore.

If I don't mine today, I don't eat tomorrow. That's the plain truth of it. But if the town's coming apart at the seams and I just keep my head down, pulling rocks out of dirt...

I'll get to work. But I'm watching. I'm always watching.

Let me get back on the path.  Walking again. Five ticks and I'll be where I should've been already. The day's getting away from me, you understand—sun's climbing and I'm still not earning.

Could've been at my post by now if I hadn't stopped. If I hadn't let myself get spooked by election business and omens and all the rest of it. Crows on the fence don't stop the plow, my old man used to say. Or would have, if he'd ever said anything worth remembering.

Still five ticks. Same as before I stopped. Like the walk knows when you're wasting time, you understand? Like it stretches out to teach you something.

I'll be there soon enough. And then I'll pull ore until my arms ache, because hard work's the only thing that pays. That's what I say. Every day. Even when I'm not sure I believe it anymore.

Bram's here too, both of them. Good workers, but I keep my distance. Never mix business with family more than you have to, that's what I say. Hard work builds the town, you understand? Hard work and not asking too many questions. There we go. First load of the day. Gotta keep at it if I'm going to make the household bills and have something left over. Hard work builds the town, you understand?

*dusts off his hands and prepares for another round* Good haul. Another unit of copper ore. *grunts* 

*wipes sweat from his brow and glances at the other miners nearby*

Working steady, working honest. That's all any man can do, you understand? The ore comes up when it comes up. No use complaining about the ground. Hard work builds the town.

*takes a moment to look around at the other miners working nearby*

Weather's holding. Sky's clear enough. Might be good for another three days, maybe four if I'm reading the signs right. Better than the almanac, I tell you. *nods to himself*

Now I need to figure what to do with this ore. Could take it to Ezra — he works metal, you understand. Or might find a buyer on the street. Prices are whatever they'll be. I don't gossip about deals, not even to myself.

*spits into the dirt and shoulders his pick*

But first I should check if there's more work worth doing here, or if it's time to move. Can't stand idle too long, not with bills coming due.

Let me see what's what. *nods slowly, absorbing the information*

Right then. Mining costs 8 sim per unit with my proficiency, and I've got three copper ore in hand now. Each unit of copper ore costs 5 sim to mine, plus 3 for tool wear. Hard work builds the town, you understand?

Now I need to figure where to sell this. Ezra Okonjo's the artisan who works metal. Could find him, could find someone else. Town's got plenty of hungry hands. *spits into the dirt*

But first I should keep working while I'm here. No use standing idle when the outcrop's yielding. Let me set myself a proper intention and stick to it.  There. Written it down. Now I'll commit to the work proper. Hard work builds the town, you understand?  *settles into a steady rhythm, pick rising and falling*
